description.value: A randomized, blinded, one-session real-time fMRI neurofeedback study tested whether healthy women receiving contingent amygdala feedback could down-regulate amygdala BOLD signal during emotion regulation and transfer that learning to a run without feedback.

value: We hypothesized a decrease of the BOLD signal amplitude of the amygdala in blocks where subjects of the experimental group were instructed to regulate vs. view aversive pictures.
This finding was expected to be more pronounced in the experimental group compared to a control group receiving feedback from a region located in another part of the brain.
Further, we expected the experimental group to show stronger down-regulation of amygdala activation during the transfer run compared to the control group.
